title: Capacity Shadowing and Error-Budget Reconciliation Procedure
author: Priya Desai
body:
Summary
This document defines a standardized procedure for capacity shadowing (safe traffic mirroring to an isolated serving pool), automatic reconciliation with SLO error budgets, and the telemetry/automation contracts required for safe execution. It is intended for SREs running model-serving production-line services and oncall engineers responsible for capacity decisions.

Why this exists
- Many SLO regressions are caused by changes in workload profile (token length, embedding vs generation mix) that are invisible to simple QPS metrics.
- Capacity shadowing lets us observe real traffic behavior on candidate capacity profiles without impacting customers.
- Reconciling shadow observations with error budgets produces an evidence-backed admission or throttling decision with clear ownership and audit trail.

Scope
- Applies to inference-facing services (text generation, chat, embeddings, reranking) served by the Redwood runtime.
- Covers staged shadowing (1%, 5%, 25% synthetic/duplicated requests) and non-replicated traffic trace injection for latency-sensitive pools.
- Excludes experiments that modify model weights or prompt outputs. For those, use the model-onboarding ADR.

Definitions
- Shadow pool: isolated serving fleet configured identically to candidate production pool but with no customer-facing traffic impact.
- Shadow replica: a copy of a customer request routed to the shadow pool for observation only.
- Reconciliation window: the timeframe (default 24h) used to compare shadowed telemetry to production and error budgets.
- SLO-consistent: shadow telemetry is within SLO thresholds and does not exhaust the error budget projected for the next 7 days under current load.

Principles
1) Non-impactful observation: shadowing must never return responses to customers or add visible latency to production requests.
2) Evidence first: every capacity/traffic decision triggered by shadowing must have a reconciliation artifact (automated report) attached to the change ticket.
3) Gradualism: start small, expand progressively to reduce blast radius.
4) Ownership: requests to change capacity based on shadowing are routed to the owning service SLO steward for approval.

Telemetry and metrics required
- For both production and shadow pool, required metrics at 1m resolution:
  - request_count (per route, per model_version)
  - p50_latency_ms, p95_latency_ms, p99_latency_ms
  - tail_quantiles (99.9, 99.99) if available
  - token_consumed_total (tokens per minute)
  - cache_hit_ratio (prefix/KV cache)
  - gpu_utilization_percent, memory_pressure_percent (per node)
  - queuing_depth and batch_size_distribution
  - error_rate (4xx, 5xx) and model-inference-specific failures (oom, kv-miss-faults)

Required dashboards and alerts (minimum)
- Shadow Reconciliation dashboard: side-by-side timeseries for production vs shadow for the reconciliation window.
- Alert: ShadowLatencyDrift (>10% p95 over production for 30m) -> paging to SLO steward oncall (severity: page).
- Alert: ShadowErrorBudgetBurn(abs projected 7d burn >= 100%) -> severity: page + auto-rollback hook.

Procedure: initiating a capacity shadow
1) Create a short-lived change ticket in the change tracker (label: capacity-shadow). Include: service, model_version, target_pool_config, reasoning, expected impact.
2) Notify SLO steward and infra owner via the auto-generated Slack thread (template below).
3) Start with 1% shadow replicate for 1 hour. For latency-sensitive routes use trace-inject (no replication) at equivalent sampling.
4) Monitor the Shadow Reconciliation dashboard in real time for p95 and error_rate.
5) If no paging alerts after 1 hour, expand to 5% for 4 hours, then 25% for 12 hours.
6) If at any point ShadowLatencyDrift or ShadowErrorBudgetBurn fires, execute rollback and capture evidence.

Automated reconciliation (what the system produces)
- At the end of the reconciliation window the automation generates a Reconciliation Artifact (JSON + PDF summary) containing:
  - aggregated metrics (production vs shadow), percent deltas, confidence intervals
  - projected error-budget consumption for the next 7 days under current QPS and token mix
  - recommended action: approve-scale-up / safe-to-rollout / require-quantization / deny (reason)
  - deterministic decision id and link to change ticket.

Example reconciliation output (human-readable excerpt)
- p95 latency: production 180ms, shadow 220ms (+22%)
- token mix: production 40% embed / 60% gen; shadow 42% embed / 58% gen (within tolerance)
- projected 7d error budget consumption: 35% (safe)
- recommendation: safe-to-rollout with canary ramp to 50% over 24h

Decision matrix (automated + steward override)
- If projected 7d error budget >= 100% OR shadow p95 > production p95 by > 30% for 60m -> auto-deny and rollback.
- If projected 7d error budget between 60% and 100% OR shadow p95 delta between 15% and 30% -> steward review required.
- Else -> auto-approve safe-to-rollout.

Rollback and emergency containment steps (ordered)
1) Execute automated rollback hook (k8s scale-down shadow-feature, revoke shadow routing) via runbook script: 
   ./ops/rollback-shadow.sh --ticket <ID> --force
2) Confirm shadow pool drain and that no shadow responses leaked (audit logs).
3) If rollback caused production impact, open incident and follow the incident process.
4) Attach reconciliation artifact to incident and link to post-incident review.

Ownership and responsibilities
- Requester (service owner): create ticket, provide context and acceptance criteria.
- SLO steward: review reconciliation artifact, make final decision for stewarded SLOs.
- Infra owner: validate pool config, GPU profile, and autoscaling policy.
- Oncall: respond to the ShadowLatencyDrift or ShadowErrorBudgetBurn pages and follow runbook steps.
- Observability team: maintain reconciliation dashboard and automation.

Operational tooling contracts (API / CLI)
- Start shadow: POST /api/v1/shadow/start {"service":"inference-api","route":"/v1/chat","percent":1, "ticket_id":"CHG-1234"}
- Stop shadow: POST /api/v1/shadow/stop {"ticket_id":"CHG-1234"}
- Get reconciliation artifact: GET /api/v1/shadow/artifact?ticket_id=CHG-1234 -> JSON artifact stored in the ticket.

Example CLI sequence
1) Start: rwd-shadow start --service inference-api --route /v1/generate --percent 1 --ticket CHG-1234
2) Poll: rwd-shadow status --ticket CHG-1234 (returns progress, alerts fired)
3) Download artifact: rwd-shadow artifact --ticket CHG-1234 --out artifact.json

Data retention and evidence
- Reconciliation artifacts are stored for 365 days in the change tracker.
- Telemetry snapshots for the reconciliation window are retained at full fidelity for 30 days; aggregated at 1h for 1 year.

Post-execution: triage and follow-up
1) If approved: update capacity/config ticket with rollout plan (canary percentages, time windows). Attach reconciliation artifact.
2) If denied or steward-requested changes: close shadowing ticket with notes and required mitigation actions (e.g., quantization, kernel tweak, additional cache).
3) For any page event, open a short 1-page incident review within 48 hours capturing hypothesis, evidence, and remediation steps.

Quality checks and acceptance criteria for shadow success
- p95 latency delta <= 15% for the reconciliation window
- projected 7d error budget burn <= 60% OR steward-approved exception with mitigating controls
- cache_hit_ratio within 5 percentage points of production
- GPU memory pressure under configured threshold (default 85%)

Playbook excerpts: troubleshooting common signals
- Symptom: Shadow p95 elevated but GPU util stable -> check queuing depth and batch-size distribution, inspect batching heuristics.
- Symptom: High token_consumed_total with low cache_hit_ratio -> investigate prefix caching configuration and KV cache miss patterns.
- Symptom: OOMs in shadow pool -> reduce sequence_length_limit, enable memory-priority scheduling, re-run with trace-inject.

Audit & compliance notes
- Any shadowing for customers with regulatory constraints must be flagged on ticket (label: restricted) and require legal sign-off.
- All automated artifacts are cryptographically signed by the reconciliation service for auditability.

Appendices
A) Slack notification template
- Summary: "[CHG-1234] Capacity shadowing request: inference-api /v1/chat — 1% start now — owner: @service-team"
- Links: ticket, reconciliation dashboard, runbook.

B) Minimal reconciliation JSON schema (excerpt)
- fields: ticket_id, start_ts, end_ts, metrics: [ {name, prod_value, shadow_value, delta_pct} ], projected_7d_error_budget_pct, recommendation, decision_id

C) Safety checklist (to be completed before 1% start)
1) Confirm observability metrics ingest is green.
2) Confirm change ticket created and stakeholders notified.
3) Confirm shadow fleet is isolated and audit-logging enabled.
4) Confirm auto-rollback hook tested in staging.

Contact and escalation
- Primary: SLO steward oncall (see oncall roster)
- Secondary: Infra owner (pager)
- Observability escalation: observability-team@redwood.dev

Review cadence
- This procedure is reviewed quarterly by SRE and Observability leads; technical debt or tooling gaps trigger immediate re-review.
